title: Addition Equations Worksheets: True or False
intro: Use true-or-false equations to teach the meaning of the equal sign.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Evaluate both sides and compare their values. Ask the student to explain equality rather than treating the sign as a signal to write an answer.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

4 + 3 = 8 is false.

Four counters and three more make seven counters. Seven and eight are different amounts, so the two sides do not have the same value.

Ask your student

Do both sides name the same amount?

If your student needs help

If the student assumes every printed equation is true, model a counterexample with counters.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each set contains three true and three false original equations in a varying order. Addends range from 2 through 9. Correct sums range from 4 through 18, and the displayed right-hand number can be as large as 19.
